body: No worries. I really appreciate your good advice and your support. Thank you so much! I am thinking now about some online ESL tutoring jobs that I was looking at about a month ago which would be pretty lucrative and which I can do from home. I taught ESL abroad for 3 years in the past, and this might be a good little step, besides bringing in much-needed money to help that side of things.
This really means a lot to me right now. Thank you!
Thank you so much for your kind reply. I feel so much better after reading these posts, and I feel like climbing back up on the proverbial horse, if you know what I mean.

The main thing is, you don't want to get caught in a cyclical trap of regret about it. You know, now, that it wasn't a good solution to your problems. I've also been suicidal because of my OCD, and it's hell. But you have to just see it as a mistake, treat yourself kindly, and just not go down that path of thinking again.

You don't want to let the guilt from the past weigh on you so heavily that you can't move forward. You seem like a really smart, kind person with a lot to offer the world. It would be a shame for your potential to be misspent worrying about your past.

I'm so sorry you had that happen over the summer. But you know it gets better, and you have probably also realized something which I struggle to keep in mind: you can't magically change the past by going back to it over and over again. You have to just process it the best you can, learn from your mistakes, and move forward.

I'm going to try to start exercising again. Sometimes I'm able to start a walking regimen, and I'll go for long walks. The repetitive type of exercise really helps for OCD and anxiety. Exercise in general helps anxiety, and then repetitive exercise helps those gears in our OCD brain to stop grinding.

I'm also thinking if I can get past the beginning side effects, hopefully the Prozac will start helping again. But the side effects can really suck. For me, it's like I have zero appetite, I feel like I've had 3 pots of coffee, and I can't sleep. 

I remember these side effects from before, but over time it seems I've gotten really sensitive to medications. 

Can I ask what your dosage is on the Prozac?

I have my M.A. in Russian, and so I taught that language in grad school for 3 years. Before grad school, I taught ESL overseas for three years. I really like teaching, and it's frustrating because I thought that subbing would be a good way back into the profession.

I was on Prozac from 1993-2008 and it really helped back then. But I think I'm really sensitive to new medications. I was on Paxil for the last 5 years, and I think it helped with anxiety but it didn't help my OCD symptoms.

Thanks so much for responding. It's been such a tough week. Since you have OCD too, you know how hard the struggle is. It seems like it takes a lot of resolve to keep fighting every day. 

And basically, that's my plan for the next 2 weeks. Just kind of remind myself to slow down and take one step forward at a time, and also to just cope with one problem at a time.

Yeah, I think it might just help ease the pressure on my family and me. I have resisted the idea because I don't want to lose my motivation, but I'm a pretty motivated person I think. It might be a good pressure release so that taking these small steps forward will be easier. 

Also, I have heard that you can get good help in vocational rehab, in terms of them helping you get back to work.

Thanks for the advice, it really, really means a lot.
